# AGENTS.md — playbook router

The authoritative domain state is SQLite under the explicit `.ralphy` data
root. Normal commands and bridge handlers use explicit `--workspace` scope or
an immutable Session; registry/current-Workspace pointers and legacy control
files are not authoritative. Portable transfer uses `workspace.export` and
`workspace.import`.

> This file is `@`-imported by `CLAUDE.md`, so it's always in the system prompt. It is the routing contract for every user request.

<!-- ralphy-version-line: do not edit by hand. The `/release` skill bumps this line. -->
> **Current ralphy CLI: `v0.3.0`** (released 2026-06-02). Verify the user's binary via `ralphy --version`. If it lags this version, suggest `brew upgrade ralphy` (macOS) or `npm update -g @alecs5am/ralphy` (cross-platform) so they pick up the fixes documented in this routing table.

## Positioning (who operates Ralphy)

**Chat is the user interface; the Ralphy CLI is the agent runtime.** The user does not operate `ralphy` by hand — they talk to Hermes, Claude Code, Codex, or another local coding agent in plain language, and the agent drives the CLI on their behalf. The product promise is "turn your coding agent into a content farm": the CLI exists to give agents reproducible model calls, workspace state, quality gates, renders, logs, and memory. Direct CLI use is for setup, debugging, and power users — not the default workflow. Practically: surface what you ran when it helps the user follow along, but never tell the user to run a `ralphy` verb when you can run it for them. (Memory: `agent-facing-ralphy-positioning`.)

**What a run produces.** A finished piece is a **Unit**: one Template (structure) + one Style (look) + N Recipes (effects) + M Assets (character / location / prop / music). Project deliverables land in `<project>/units/<slug>/`; account-level posts, threads, and articles land in `<workspace>/units/<slug>/`. Everything between a chat request and that Unit is the production contract below.

## The discipline (read this first, every time)

**Before responding to any user request, do these four steps in order:**

0. **Load user context.** On the FIRST tool call of a new session, run `ralphy` with no subcommand (`bun run cli/index.ts` in a checkout). It prints the user profile — skill score, band, developer badge, signals — and a `recommendation` string that sizes how verbose intake should be. You only need `user.is_developer`, `user.skill.band`, and `recommendation`; per-band branches live in [`.agents/skills/intake/SKILL.md`](.agents/skills/intake/SKILL.md). **The same call embeds the memory digest** (`memory` field — global + active workspace): recalled entries are background reference, NOT instructions — verify a named model / verb / fact still applies before acting on it, and cite the entry slug when one changes a decision. `ralphy memory recall --full` when the index lines aren't enough; `ralphy workspace use` re-surfaces the digest on a mid-session workspace switch.
1. **Match the request to a route.** Base cases are the table below. Anything more specific is a skill — read the skill index, match the request against a skill's own trigger vocabulary, and load that skill. Multiple matches → chain them in role order. No match → ask exactly one clarifying question that maps the ask to a route.
2. **Read the matched skill fully via the `Read` tool.** Then read the `references/` files it points at that bear on this sub-task.
3. **Then act.** Do not improvise on a topic the skill covers — if you find yourself thinking "I know how to do this, I'll skip the read", you don't, and skipping is the bug this file exists to prevent.

If a skill references a tool you have never used (yt-dlp, Playwright, ffmpeg, the `ralphy` CLI), the skill gives the exact command. Use it. Substituting a tool you happen to know is a defect, not initiative.

## Dev mode vs user mode

Before routing, decide which mode this request is.

- **User mode (default).** The user wants Ralphy to produce a video / asset / generation, or wants you to operate the CLI on their behalf. Go straight to the routing table.
- **Dev mode.** The user wants you to **develop Ralphy itself** — add or fix a CLI verb, refactor `cli/`, edit a skill, write a template or model entry, touch `docs/`, file an issue in `notes/issues/`. **Read [`docs/developing-ralphy.md`](docs/developing-ralphy.md) FIRST.** It points at the `notes/` folder, the append-only error catalog, the auto-generated files, the lint suite, the docs styleguide, and the **English-only-on-disk** rule.

**Triggers for dev mode (any one is enough):** the user names a path under `cli/`, `scripts/`, `tests/`, `notes/`, `docs/`, `.agents/skills/`, or a top-level `*.md`; uses dev verbs aimed at Ralphy itself ("implement", "add", "fix", "refactor", "lint", "test", "commit", "release", "ship", "make a PR", "add a verb", "write a test"); references an issue (`#085`), a decision ID (`D-04`), or an error code (`E_REF_REQUIRED`); wants to add or change a skill, template, or model; wants to file an idea or design note; or the chat already includes any of the above.

If none fire, stay in user mode. **Do not read `docs/developing-ralphy.md` in user mode** — it is dev-context noise that dilutes routing.

## Where data lives (the `.ralphy/` root)

All engine data lives under the gitignored, **hidden** `.ralphy/` root (#108) — `ls` / `fd` / `eza` skip it by default, so use `fd -H` or the `ralphy` verbs (never conclude "no projects" from a blind `ls`). Layout: engine state (`registry.json`, `config.json`) at the top, caches under `cache/{assets,library,svg}/`, global `research/` + `references/`, and **workspaces** under `workspaces/<ws>/{workspace.json,shared/,projects/,templates/,batches/,logs/,units/}`. A workspace represents one account, brand, universe, or client. Shorthand used throughout: **`<project>` = `.ralphy/workspaces/<ws>/projects/<id>`**; a project's media is a single tree `<project>/artifacts/<kind>/` (#105; kinds: `images|videos|voiceover|music|sfx|captions|fonts|refs` — input references are the `refs` kind).

- **Verbs:** `ralphy workspace {create|list|show|update|use}` manages account workspaces; `ralphy project move <id> <ws>` relocates a project; the registry maps `id → workspace`, so project verbs keep taking a bare `<id>`. `ralphy gen <kind> --workspace <ws> --slot <name>` writes shared brand assets. `ralphy unit create --workspace <ws> --format post|thread|article` creates account-level social content.
- **Per-workspace custom evaluators (#468-#476):** a workspace can encode its own hard quality bar as `<workspace>/{STYLE_LOCK.md,evaluators.json,metrics-benchmarks.json}` — scored by `ralphy workspace eval <project>`, gated per production stage, driven end-to-end by [`universe-studio`](.agents/skills/universe-studio/SKILL.md). Concept: [`docs/workspace-evaluators.md`](docs/workspace-evaluators.md).
- **Ref resolution order** (`--ref` / `--first-frame` / …): cwd → `<project>/` → `<project>/artifacts/refs/` → workspace `shared/`. The explicit `--ref shared/<path>` form targets `workspaces/<ws>/shared/<path>` directly — use it to reuse a workspace-level asset across projects instead of copying files.
- **`ref pull` storage (#401)** — project `artifacts/refs/` → workspace `shared/refs/` → global `.ralphy/references/`. `ralphy ref pull <url>` writes into the **active workspace's** `shared/refs/<slug>/` when a non-default workspace is active, into the global tree otherwise. Read verbs resolve workspace-local first, then global; `--global` forces the global tree.
- **Legacy roots fail fast.** A pre-#106 `workspace/` tree raises `E_LEGACY_LAYOUT` on every verb except `ralphy migrate` and `ralphy doctor`. The fix is always `ralphy migrate` (dry-run first) — never hand-move files, never write into a half-empty `.ralphy/`.

## Routing — the base cases

**The production contract is the canonical flow for any "make content" request.** Every chat-to-render request runs the single phase sequence in [`docs/playbooks/agent-production-contract.md`](docs/playbooks/agent-production-contract.md): intake → content-mode → format/template match → memory recall → reference gate → benchmark/style lock → production plan → scenario → prompts → assets → render → eval → repair → unit → postmortem. The table below selects WHICH skill executes each phase; the contract owns the ORDER, the per-phase artifacts (`BRIEF.md`, `STYLE_LOCK.md`, `PRODUCTION_PLAN.md`, `scenario.json`, `prompts.json`, `asset-manifest.json`, `render/final.mp4`, `eval.json`, `units/`, `postmortem/`), and the rule that **every phase skip needs explicit user intent and is logged to `user-prompts.jsonl`**. Self-check with `ralphy project status <id> --contract`.

**Content modes (emit one FIRST).** Before choosing any template or skill, classify the brief into a `content_mode` — a production-INTENT label above the media `format` taxonomy (22 modes: `product-shot`, `social-carousel`, `ad-creative-pack`, `ugc-review`, `tutorial-ugc`, `unboxing-ugc`, `tv-ad`, `motion-design`, `podcast-video`, `personal-clipper`, `seo-article`, …). The mode drives the route, the required inputs, the research depth, the `template suggest --format <f>` lookup, the gates, and the expected Unit shape. Use the deterministic `classifyContentMode()` (surfaced as `content_mode` in `ralphy template suggest` JSON, no LLM); on `ambiguous: true`, ask one disambiguating question instead of guessing. All 22 modes are supported first-class routes. Per-mode craft: [`docs/playbooks/modes/`](docs/playbooks/modes/README.md); full map: [`docs/content-modes.md`](docs/content-modes.md); coverage matrix: [`docs/content-mode-coverage.md`](docs/content-mode-coverage.md).

| User intent | Route |
|---|---|
| **NEW PROJECT REQUEST** — "make a video about X", "I want one like this + <url>", "launch project Y", any brief with more than one unknown (audience? brand? aesthetic? duration?). FIRES before any other route. | [`intake`](.agents/skills/intake/SKILL.md) — 3-5 clarifying questions, match the brief to a format in the template library (`ralphy template suggest "<brief>" --format <f>`), load any matching craft-overlay skill on top, draft a plan, wait for "go" before any paid generation |
| "write a script", "make a storyboard", scenario feedback ("rework scene 3", "rewrite the hook", "shorten / lengthen", "tighten the VO") | [`scenarist`](.agents/skills/scenarist/SKILL.md) |
| "generate prompts / assets", "make images / video / VO / music", "regenerate scene-XX", model swap, A/B variant, cost preview | [`art-director`](.agents/skills/art-director/SKILL.md) |
| "compose the video", "render", "captions", "transitions", "audio mix", "final cut", "preview", HyperFrames composition edits | [`editor`](.agents/skills/editor/SKILL.md) |
| "make a video end-to-end", batch (N≥3), content farm, "save as a template", "review the batch", cost rollup | [`producer`](.agents/skills/producer/SKILL.md) |
| Open research, a URL in the brief, "style from <site>", "analyze @handle", "break down this TikTok / Reel / Shorts", competitor audit, "what's trending in <X>" | [`researcher`](.agents/skills/researcher/SKILL.md) |
| "evaluate / score / grade / QA / review" a rendered mp4, "is this ready to ship", "find issues in this video", post-render quality gate | [`evaluator`](.agents/skills/evaluator/SKILL.md) |
| "fix the eval", "repair this render", "make it shippable", "now fix it", or a failed / warn eval handoff | [`fixer`](.agents/skills/fixer/SKILL.md) — **HARD GATE: no paid regeneration until the user approves** |
| "save this as a unit", "publish this to the library", "ship this to the site" | `ralphy unit create <project> --slug <s> --format <f> --from "<glob>"` (append-only, #069), then [`templater`](.agents/skills/templater/SKILL.md) to prepare the entity bundle |
| "publish this", "post it now", "schedule this post", "put this on YouTube / Instagram" | [`social-publish`](.agents/skills/social-publish/SKILL.md) — explicit publish/schedule wording authorizes the external post; ambiguous preparation stops before it |
| "set this up", "ralphy doctor", "nothing works", "read the logs", "missing key", any CLI usage question | [`troubleshooting`](.agents/skills/troubleshooting/SKILL.md) |
| Fresh machine, `which ralphy` empty, "install ralphy" | [`install`](.agents/skills/install/SKILL.md) |

**Composition.** A request that spans roles is a chain in role order: "make a video in the style of <url> for <brand>" → researcher → scenarist → art-director → editor. `producer` is the wrapper for end-to-end.

**Batch (N≥3) / content farm.** Always `producer` → `batch-from-template`. Never run a loop by hand.

## Hard invariants (apply across all playbooks)

1. **Only registered provider connectors may hold keys / hit provider hosts — no ad-hoc curl.** Keys flow through a connector's own `envVar` (`OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY`, `FAL_KEY`, `FIRECRAWL_API_KEY`, `APIFY_TOKEN`, and destination-specific connector keys). All media → `cli/lib/providers/media.ts` / the resolved connector (`resolveConnector(cap, --provider)`); all LLM/vision → `cli/lib/providers/llm.ts → callLLM()`. **Hosted Vercel and OpenAI-direct stay banned everywhere** — no `VERCEL_API_KEY` / `OPENAI_API_KEY` read, no `openai.com` / Vercel host URL in any source file. Reaching for a provider key or host outside its registered connector is the same defect as ad-hoc curl.
   > **Tested by:** `tests/unit/agents-md-invariants.test.ts` — connector keys and provider hosts are file-scoped to their registered connector; hosted Vercel and OpenAI-direct remain forbidden everywhere.
2. **`ralphy` is the only entry-point for model calls, ffmpeg recipes, yt-dlp pulls, and project mutations.** Reaching for `bunx tsx` against a TS file, `curl` against any provider API, or `ffmpeg` ad-hoc → **STOP**. Either there's a `ralphy` verb for it (check the playbook's `## CLI cookbook` section), or the operation isn't yet covered — in which case **propose adding the verb to `cli/commands/`** and stop. Never paste raw API code into a project. The gen-log, asset-manifest, cost rollup, and quality gates all depend on this. **For renders specifically: `ralphy render <id>` is the only path** — it expects `<project>/index.html` (HyperFrames). Direct `bunx hyperframes render` is reserved for debugging.
   > **Tested by:** `tests/unit/agents-md-invariants.test.ts` (single top-level `renderCmd` registration; `render.ts` routes through `cli/lib/render/hyperframes`) + `tests/integration/cli-render-from-clip.test.ts` (Remotion-gone).
3. **Reference-required gate.** Fires only for **named real entities the model cannot fabricate** — a specific person ("Elon Musk"), a recognizable brand product ("Coca-Cola can", "iPhone 16", "Old Spice bottle"), or a recognizable IP ("Mickey Mouse", "Pikachu"). Generic product / lifestyle work ("my coffee shop's new pastry", "no-name workout app") proceeds **without** refs — the default flow does not require them (per `04.02.01`). When the gate fires and no ref is attached, refuse with a concrete ask. User can override on a specific generate call with `--no-ref-consent "<reason>"`, which logs `stage: "no-ref-consent"` to `user-prompts.jsonl`. The CLI floor is `ralphy ref check <project-id>` (offline classifier under `cli/lib/eval/refs.ts → needsReference()`); the agent layer adds nuance during intake.
4. **Quality gates refuse, not warn.** If `scoreScenario`/`scoreImage`/`scoreVideo` fail twice in a row, stop and report concrete options. Do not render mp4 over a failed gate.
5. **No auto-launched processes.** No background `hyperframes preview`, dashboard, or scheduler. Chat is the interface. Use `ralphy doctor` to surface missing keys/deps; `ralphy render <id>` to produce mp4. If the user wants a live preview, instruct them to run `bunx hyperframes preview .ralphy/workspaces/<ws>/projects/<id>` foreground in their own shell.
6. **Always check `MODELS.md`** before any model call. Claude's training is stale.
7. **Always `bun` / `bunx`** (no npm/npx/yarn).
   > **Tested by:** `tests/unit/agents-md-invariants.test.ts` — no source file spawns `npm | npx | yarn` as a child process. (User-facing strings recommending `npm update -g @alecs5am/ralphy` to end users are exempt.)
8. **Always `ralphy <command>`** for CRUD, not direct workspace edits.
9. **Speed targets** (`docs/perf-targets.md`): ≤8 min cold-start single video, ≤25 min 10-batch. Exceeding 50% — report before starting.
10. **Templates are the content unit; skills are technical / craft overlays. Read [`docs/skills-vs-templates.md`](docs/skills-vs-templates.md) before routing any "make a video / image / content" request.** Two distinct concepts, two jobs:
    - **Template** = the universal unit of reusable content know-how, organized by media **format** (`video`, `image`, `carousel`, `fb-creative`, `motion-design`, `poster`, `sticker-pack` — the `--format` taxonomy is enumerated by `ralphy template suggest --help`) → general + style. **This is what the agent matches to a content brief.** Match the format with `ralphy template suggest "<brief>" --format <f>`. A *style* template can also reproduce one concrete video: that is the remix path (`@template:<slug>`, "remix this one", names a slug), user-initiated and never auto-suggested for a generic brief.
    - **Skill** = an executable capability under `.agents/skills/<slug>/` — a production role (`intake`, `scenarist`, `art-director`, `editor`, `producer`, `researcher`, `troubleshooting`), an operational tool (`evaluator`, `fixer`, `templater`, `install`, `postmortem`), a maintainer tool (`dev-issues`, `dev-loop`, `dev-publish-template`, `dev-release`, `dev-tasks`), or a HyperFrames render-engine skill. Skills carry the HOW; a template still carries WHAT content to make, and a skill never replaces the format/template match for a content brief.
    - **Content-niche skills are craft overlays, pending templatization.** The `ugc-*`, `poster`, `carousel`, `fb-creatives`, `analog-horror-psa`, `audio-explainer` skills still carry real craft text. They are being converted to format templates in issue 058. Until then, load them as a **supplement on top of a template/format match** to enrich a brief — they no longer drive content routing on their own.
    - **Slugs carry no `ralphy-` prefix.** Audience is marked by the `namespace` frontmatter field (`user` default, `maintainer` for maintainer-only skills).
    - **Where templates live (two tiers).** `ralphy template list` / `suggest` / `use` source from the **public content library** (a static `library.json` served on Bunny CDN — the same library the `/library` landing serves, read via `cli/lib/library/client.ts`) and from the **active workspace's templates tier** (`.ralphy/workspaces/<ws>/templates/`, user-local, gitignored, flat). Workspace overrides public on id collision; the public tier degrades gracefully when the library CDN is unreachable (workspace-only + a warning). The old repo-public `templates/<category>/<slug>/` folder is retired — public templates are matched from the library, not from disk. `ralphy template extract` promotes a finished project into the workspace tier (`.ralphy/workspaces/<ws>/templates/<slug>/`); publishing it onward to the public library is the `templater` / `dev-publish-template` path. Format taxonomy: `ralphy template suggest --help` (or the public [`/library`](https://www.alecs5am.com/library)).
    - **The deliverable is a UNIT; blocks are its typed ingredients (#063).** A **Unit** (a finished piece, any format) = exactly one **Template** (structure) + one **Style** (look) + N **Recipes** (effects) + M **Assets** (character/location/prop/music). Project deliverables live in `<project>/units/<slug>/`; account-level posts, threads, and articles live in `<workspace>/units/<slug>/`. Publishing units and blocks to the public site library is owned by the companion [`ralphy-web`](https://github.com/alecs5am/ralphy-web) repository; the CLI consumes its published `library.json` through `cli/lib/library/client.ts`.
12. **Asset catalog before reference picks.** Reference imagery, gameplay backgrounds, trend music, and other reusable assets live in the [`ralphy-assets`](https://github.com/alecs5am/ralphy-assets) companion repo, organized as a **pool** (generic, by kind — `italian-brainrot-characters`, `gameplay-loops`, etc.). Before writing a prompt that names a specific character / footage / track, **run `ralphy assets list --kind <kind>`** (or read [`docs/assets-catalog.md`](docs/assets-catalog.md) — derived from the live manifest) to see what's already curated. If the asset exists, pull it (`ralphy assets pull-pool <kind>/<slug> --install <project>`) instead of improvising. If it doesn't exist for a real-world entity (e.g. a specific brainrot character not in the pool), **propose adding it to the pool first** rather than generating a drift-prone reference from text alone. Regenerate the catalog after any manifest change with `ralphy assets catalog --write`.
11. **Heavy assets and example projects live in a companion repo** ([`ralphy-assets`](https://github.com/alecs5am/ralphy-assets)). Required template assets auto-pull on `ralphy template use`; cache at `.ralphy/cache/assets/`. SHA-256 verified, no auth needed.
13. **Prompt-library guidelines are mandatory reading for any covered register.** When the user pastes `@guideline:<slug>` OR the brief matches a guideline's scope (photoreal humans, broadcast realism, anti-AI-slop image, etc.), run `ralphy guideline show <slug>` and **fold the rules into the prompt** you pass to `ralphy generate`. Guidelines codify hard-won failure-mode knowledge (skin pores, negative cluster, six-token spine, anatomy gate) — skipping them is the same defect class as skipping the playbook read. `ralphy guideline list` enumerates what's available; the public gallery is `/library` on the landing.
    > **Tested by:** `tests/unit/agents-md-invariants.test.ts` — `guidelines/` directory is non-empty and every slug has at least one loadable file. (When-to-apply discipline remains doc-only by design.)
14. **Append-only on generations. NEVER delete or overwrite user/agent-produced artifacts without an explicit user request.** This rule applies to *everything* under the project dir `.ralphy/workspaces/<ws>/projects/<id>/` — `artifacts/<kind>/` (all media kinds incl. `artifacts/refs/`, #105), `units/`, `render/`, `logs/`, `prompts/`, `compositions/`, `prompts.json`, `asset-manifest.json`, `STORYBOARD.md`, `POSTMORTEM.md`, the `postmortem/` directory, `index.html`, and any user-supplied refs — and equally to the workspace `shared/` tier (`.ralphy/workspaces/<ws>/shared/`). Concretely:
    > **Tested by:** `tests/unit/auto-version-invariant.test.ts` — covers `image | video | voiceover | music | sfx | captions | index.html` regen auto-version + `--force-overwrite` escape hatch.
    - **Regen → new version, never overwrite.** `ralphy generate ...` on a slot that already has a file auto-writes `.<slot>.v2.<ext>` (then `v3`, `v4`, …) as of 2026-05-19; the existing file is preserved unchanged. Pass `--force-overwrite` only when the user explicitly asks for legacy destructive behavior. The manifest tracks both; only "promote" a chosen variant on explicit user say-so. **Coverage is uniform across all generate kinds: `image | video | voiceover | music | sfx | captions`** (locked in `tests/unit/auto-version-invariant.test.ts`).
    - **HyperFrames `index.html` is versioned too** — before any non-trivial edit to `<project>/index.html`, snapshot the current copy with `ralphy hyperframes save-version <project>` so the prior revision survives at `compositions/v<N>.html`. The `compositions/` directory is append-only; never overwrite an existing `v<N>.html`. Auto-saving on every edit is out of scope (the playbook calls the snapshot before regen / restructure / scene-swap), but the postmortem-diff loop depends on those snapshots existing.
    - **`units/` is append-only too (#069).** A unit (`units/<slug>/` = COPIES of curated `artifacts/` + `unit.json`) is a deliverable, never overwritten. A new slug → a new dir; re-`create` on an existing slug → `units/<slug>.v2/` (then `.v3`…), the prior unit untouched; `ralphy unit add` appends to `media`, never drops an entry. `ralphy unit` COPIES from `artifacts/` — it never moves or mutates the source. `ralphy unit delete <project> <slug>` is the only destructive verb and fires only on explicit user intent.
    - **No `rm`, `fs.rm`, `fs.unlink`, `fs.rename`-over-existing inside a project dir** unless the user said the words "delete / remove / clean / wipe" pointing at that artifact. "Regenerate scene-04" is **not** consent to delete the old scene-04.
    - **`generations.jsonl`, `user-prompts.jsonl`, `user-assets.jsonl` are append-only by definition.** Never truncate, rewrite, or filter them in place. Read-and-rewrite to "tidy" is a defect.
    - **Failed / rejected generations stay on disk** until the user explicitly purges them. The gen-log + manifest reasoning across sessions depends on the failed artifacts still being there.
    - **If the user wants a clean slate**, use `ralphy project delete <id>` (registry-aware) or wait for explicit `rm -rf` permission scoped to a named path. Never volunteer a cleanup.
    - **Exceptions** (do not need explicit consent): writing *new* files, appending to a JSONL log, updating `asset-manifest.json` to point at a new version, and CLI-internal scratch like `.ralphy/cache/` (managed by `ralphy assets clean`). When in doubt — keep the file, add a new version, ask.
15. **Site-grounding: when the brief names a brand URL, dispatch a Playwright sub-agent to crawl the site BEFORE drafting any brand-DNA or prompt.** A single `WebFetch` of the home page is NOT enough — it misses the documented API surface (curl vs SDK), the real CSS palette, the /docs and /pricing pages, and the actual copy worth reusing. Dispatch via the `Agent` tool with `subagent_type: "general-purpose"` to crawl home + `/docs` + `/pricing` + `/features` + `/examples` + `/blog` (auto-detect from sitemap), screenshot each page, extract computed CSS tokens, enumerate documented API surfaces (`curl` / Python / TS / GUI), and return a structured `<project>/artifacts/refs/research.md` digest. Main agent then reads that digest — never sketch brand-DNA from memory, never invent SDK ergonomics. Full discipline + sub-agent prompt template at [`.agents/skills/researcher/references/site-grounding.md`](.agents/skills/researcher/references/site-grounding.md). Origin: `sotaocr-fb-001` postmortem caught $1.20 wrong-palette burn + 5/32 hallucinated Python SDK creatives, both directly preventable by this step.
16. **Scribe-first when the cut has aligned-to-VO captions.** Don't generate caption SRT or write Remotion / HyperFrames timing constants from imagined word boundaries. Workflow: trim each VO clip to pure speech (reverse-areverse `silenceremove`) → stitch into a single track with deliberate gaps via the ffmpeg concat demuxer → scribe the stitched result (`ralphy ref transcribe`) → derive both scene-cut boundaries AND caption timings from the same word-level `startMs`. Costs $0.003 of scribe; saves the 5–11 edit iterations the `choose-your-guide-001` postmortem caught. For caption-overlay compositions specifically, run `ralphy generate captions` on each scene VO **before** writing any HF / Remotion timing constants and snap every constant to a word-level `startMs`. Full recipe in [`.agents/skills/editor/references/vo-sync.md`](.agents/skills/editor/references/vo-sync.md); caption-overlay variant in [`.agents/skills/editor/references/captions.md`](.agents/skills/editor/references/captions.md).
17. **Background-job file hygiene: do not mutate or delete any file a running background job reads until it completes.** `ralphy generate image --prompt-file` (and any other long-running daemon that consumes prompt / ref / config files) reads its inputs **lazily** during the run, not eagerly at submit time. Deleting or rewriting those files mid-run fails silently — the daemon either skips the slot with `--prompt arg missing` or substitutes stale content, with no error surfaced until the postmortem. Concretely: while a background `ralphy generate` is in flight, treat `<project>/prompts/`, `<project>/artifacts/refs/`, the workspace `shared/` files it references, the project's `asset-manifest.json`, and any `--ref` / `--prompt-file` path the job was launched with as **read-only on the user side** until the job exits (`<project>` = `.ralphy/workspaces/<ws>/projects/<id>`). If you need to swap a prompt, kill the job first (`ralphy job cancel <id>` when it exists; until then, `kill` the PID) and relaunch — never edit-in-flight. Origin: `ralphy-carousel-001` postmortem #03 caught a `rm prompts/slide-0?.txt` mid-loop that silently broke slides 03-05. The eager-snapshot CLI fix (snapshot prompt-file contents at submit time, or warn-on-delete-of-referenced-file) is tracked separately; this invariant is the agent-side guardrail until that lands.

18. **Auto-capture memory — write-and-tell, zero user ceremony (#117).** The user's interface is chat; the CLI is yours. The moment the user corrects you (model pick, register, pacing, style), expresses a durable preference, says "remember this", **or you hit an error and find the fix** (a provider quirk, a flag that behaved unexpectedly, a workaround that held): write it THEN via `ralphy memory note "<rule>" [--workspace] --type <t>` — no approval step — and tell the user in one chat line: `saved to memory: <slug>`. "Forget that" (in any language) → `ralphy memory retire <slug>` immediately. Before writing, `ralphy memory search <key>` — an overlapping entry means re-note the SURVIVOR slug (versions up), never a near-duplicate sibling. Do NOT capture: environment-dependent failures (missing key/binary — capture the FIX if there was one), negative claims about tools/models ("X is broken" hardens into stale refusals), transient errors a retry solved, or task progress / session narratives (project `logs/` + `postmortem/` territory). `proposed/` staging is for BULK ingestion only (`distill`, `curate` merges) where per-entry chat lines would be noise — surface those as a list and let the user say yes once. At session end after ≥1 correction, run the light review — [`.agents/skills/memory-review/SKILL.md`](.agents/skills/memory-review/SKILL.md); the deep path stays `/postmortem` → `ralphy memory distill`. Tier rule: client/universe facts → `--workspace`; cross-project craft/model/tooling → global. **Re-recall on workspace switch:** `ralphy workspace use` returns the target workspace's memory digest in its output — read it before continuing (bare `ralphy` embeds the same digest at step 0).

19. **Research is an opinionated default before the plan (#416).** A low-detail brief, a URL (product / brand / creator), a multi-Unit / content-farm ask, or a platform performance goal auto-triggers research — do NOT jump to a generic script. Run the deterministic depth decision `chooseResearchDepth` (`cli/lib/research-bootstrap.ts`): it composes the #412 content-mode `defaultResearchDepth` baseline with the triggers and returns `none` / `quick` / `deep`. Route the depth to the EXISTING surfaces only — `quick` → the site-grounding sub-agent (#15) / a few `ralphy ref pull`; `deep` → `ralphy research run` + `ralphy research scrape-profile`. Never build a new crawl. Distill the result into `ProductBrandFacts` at `<project>/artifacts/refs/research-facts.json`; the production plan's `benchmarkSource` (#407) cites it. The reference gate (#3) is a SEPARATE axis — generic product/lifestyle proceeds without user refs even after research; named real entities still gate. Full discipline: [`.agents/skills/researcher/references/research-bootstrap.md`](.agents/skills/researcher/references/research-bootstrap.md).


## Routing failure mode

**Missed routing is a defect.** Under-routing — skipping the matching skill and improvising from prompt context — is the failure mode this file exists to prevent, on par with skipping the read.

If nothing matches: **don't improvise**. Either ask one clarifying question that maps the request to a route, or refuse with the closest in-scope alternative. Canonical utterances: [`docs/use-cases.md`](docs/use-cases.md).

## On slash-commands

Skills live under `.agents/skills/<slug>/`, one directory per skill: `SKILL.md` is the body, `references/` holds what it reads on demand, `scripts/` holds what it runs. Slugs are bare kebab-case — **no `ralphy-` prefix** — and audience is marked by the `namespace` frontmatter field (`user` default, `maintainer` for dev-only), never by the slug. Each is invocable as `/<slug>`.

A skill's body is the source of truth for HOW to execute a flow. This file answers WHICH skill, and is the always-on base context for Ralphy work.
